title: Забота о маме Лёвы  (Caring for Lyova's Mother)

segments.t: In the storage room, Kostya and Nastya nearly get caught again and pretend the rustling noise was just the kitchen cat. Moments later, Chef Barinov corners Lyova and guilts his sous-chef for never taking his devoted mother out to cultural events.
Нам с тобой нужно серьезно поговорить.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'Wait a second, are you sure that...' Barinov chooses a serious mood as they talk, combining "podozhdite" ("wait") and "uverena" ("sure, confident") so the key meaning lands right away.
'Well, of course.' Kostya sustains a natural course in their talk, putting "konechno" ("of course") alongside "nu" ("oh, come on") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Come on, do not be afraid.' Lyova chooses a candid footing at this moment, combining "boysya" ("be afraid") and "da" ("yes") so the key meaning lands right away.
'I am not afraid at all.' Barinov maintains an honest note in the room, weaving "boyus" ("am afraid") together with "da" ("yes") just the way native speakers do.
'Who is in there?' Kostya inquires frankly beside Barinov, putting "tam" ("there") alongside "kto" ("who") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Just our kitchen cat.' Lyova projects an easygoing angle in front of Kostya, putting "kot" ("a boy cat, tomcat") alongside "nu" ("oh, come on") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Otherwise he will spot us.' Barinov displays a natural footing in the room, anchoring the Russian line on "uvidit" ("will see") and "to" ("that") without extra filler.
Нам с тобой нужно серьезно поговорить.
'You and I need to have a serious talk.' Kostya chooses a candid angle for Lyova, putting "nuzhno" ("necessary") alongside "seryezno" ("seriously") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'How could you, Lyova?' Barinov questions frankly to Kostya here, anchoring the Russian line on "chto" ("what") and "zh" ("after all, but") without extra filler.
'Why do you neglect your own mother like that?' Barinov prompts calmly as the talk turns, building the phrase around "mamu" ("mother, mum") and "lyubish" ("love") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'What do you mean?' Kostya checks sharply to keep things clear, letting the single Russian word "smysle" ("sense") carry the entire reaction on its own.
'Are you not ashamed of yourself, Lyova?' Barinov asks directly toward Lyova here, pairing "stydno" ("shameful") with "tebe" ("for you, to you") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Well, I will take her out sometime.' Barinov keeps a warm tone across the room, building the phrase around "svozhu" ("I bring together") and "kak-nibud" ("somehow") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Нам с тобой нужно серьезно поговорить.

That wraps up this scene as while Kostya and Nastya hide in the storage room and blame the noise on the kitchen cat, Chef Barinov guilts Lyova into taking his mother out for the evening. See you next time!
